verses.1: For the leader. For the sons of Korah. On lilies. A song.
verses.2: God is our refuge and strength, a helper in troubles that find us very severely.
verses.3: Therefore we will not fear when the earth is shaken and mountains tremble in the heart of the seas.
verses.4: Let the waters roar, let them be troubled; let the mountains tremble in his might. Selah.
verses.5: The river’s torrents gladden the city of God, the holy place of the Most High.
verses.6: God is in her midst; she will not waver. God will help her at dawn.
verses.7: Nations are in turmoil, kingdoms fall. He speaks, and the earth melts.
verses.8: The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah.
verses.9: Come, see the works of the LORD, the wonders he has placed on the earth.
verses.10: He breaks the weapons of war to the ends of the earth, shatters the bow, breaks the spear, burns shields in the fire.
verses.11: Be still and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted on the earth.
verses.12: The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah.

notes:
Notes
- v. 4: "Let the waters roar, let them be troubled" reflects the Hebrew's imperative form, which is poetic and rhetorical.
- v. 8: "The LORD of Hosts" and "the God of Jacob" reflect the compound title pattern from the glossary.
- v. 11: "Be still" renders the Hebrew "הַרְפּוּ", a form of the verb meaning "to be silent" or "to rest." The phrase is a call to reflection and acknowledgment of God’s sovereignty.
